ai.description: The Stout Sand Snake reaches 1.5 meters. It is uniform reddish-brown to dark chocolate above with a pale yellow belly. Key features include a robust build and a distinct, dark-edged rostral scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Psammophis longifrons* is best distinguished by its uniform, dark chocolate-brown dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct longitudinal stripes found in other species.
ai.habitat: The Stout Sand Snake inhabits arid and semi-arid regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically found in dry scrublands and rocky, open habitats at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Stout Sand Snake is a diurnal predator that actively hunts across open, sandy terrain, using its speed to pursue lizards and small rodents during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammophis longifrons* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–11 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically between April and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Stout Sand Snake (*Psammophis longifrons*) is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the Deccan Plateau across Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana.
